newsitem.title: USA: PictureTel off after 1997 revenue warning.
newsitem.headline: PictureTel off after 1997 revenue warning.

text.p: Shares in PictureTel Corp fell on Thursday after the company said it expected its revenue growth in 1997 to be "somewhat slower" than in previous years.

Merrill Lynch said it lowered its 1997 earnings estimate on the company to a range of $1.20-$1.25 per share from a range of $1.25-$1.40, citing expectations of revenue modestly lower than previously expected and higher research and development costs at PictureTel.
PictureTel, an Andover, Mass.-based maker of video-conferencing equipment, was off 2-7/16 at 16-3/16 by early afternoon.
Market sources said shares in VideoServer Inc, also a maker of video conferencing equipment, tumbled in sympathy with PictureTel. VideoServer was down six to 29-1/4.
Adams Harkness analyst Jonathan Stone said he lowered his rating on VideoServer Inc stock to market performer from attractive.
He cited expectations of declining sales by VideoServer to PictureTel and cut his 1997 earnings estimate on VideoServer to $0.90 a share from $0.95.

In a statement released late Wednesday with the company's fourth-quarter earnings, PictureTel Chief Executive Norman Gaut said the company expected to see strong revenue growth in 1997, though "the company believes growth will be at a somewhat slower rate than in previous years."
PictureTel said it expected slightly lower sales in the first quarter than in the fourth quarter of 1996.
It said it expected earnings for the first quarter to fall short of profit in the fourth quarter, though "good overall earnings growth" was expected for the full year.
The company said fourth-quarter revenues rose to $140.1 million from $102 million in the same period of 1995.
Revenues for the full year rose 39 percent to $482.5 million. Net income for 1996 rose 77 percent to a record $34.8 million, or $0.96 per share, from $19.6 million, or $0.56, the previous year.
